A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GUI-AIMA with the same authors and core framework. All pages, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison, despite some internal reporting inconsistencies.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI-grounding results, component ablations, convergence measurements and zoom-in error analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original experiments and adds benchmark results, head-pruning tests, larger-data ablations, verifier experiments and runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The anchor token, visual-sink selection, head aggregation, patch-label loss and two-step grounding procedure remain. v3 removes the alternative soft KL-based head-weighting variant from v1 Section 3.4 and evaluates an optional GUI-Actor verifier composition in Appendix B. The new efficient-attention discussion documents implementation without establishing that the main algorithm changed.

E1.justification: v3 adds desktop-focused GroundCUA training data while retaining the original training mixture for GUI-AIMA-lite. Evaluation expands beyond ScreenSpot-Pro, ScreenSpot-v2 and OSWorld-G to UI-Vision's basic, functional and spatial desktop tasks, MMBench-GUI-L2's basic and advanced grounding, and supplementary ScreenSpot-v1 evaluation.

E2.justification: Retained benchmark comparisons gain Qwen3-VL, GroundNext, GTA1, InfiGUI-G1 and GUI-Actor-with-verifier variants. InfiGUI-R1 additionally enters the ScreenSpot-v2 comparison, although it already appeared elsewhere in v1. Standalone GPT-4o is removed from ScreenSpot-Pro, and the new benchmark tables include additional comparators such as Holo2 and Aguvis.

E3.justification: v3 introduces the 509k-instruction training regime and larger-data ablation, verifier, timing and top/bottom-30% head-pruning protocols. The stated second-pass crop changes from 448 to 616 pixels, retaining 2× zoom. Exact counts are inconsistent: 250k versus 200k additional GroundCUA instructions, and 259k versus 254k larger-ablation examples. The unexplained OSWorld-G-Refine table label does not establish a changed test split.

E4.justification: v3 adds controls testing gradient flow through head weights, weighted labels for GUI-Actor, verifier compatibility and head importance through pruning. It also adds runtime analysis and token-frequency evidence, and replaces v1's embedding-versus-attention correlation examples with anchor-versus-query head-weight similarity analysis. Most original 45k ablations and zoom-error counts remain; the soft-weighting ablation is removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added experiments continue to report point estimates without uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: ScreenSpot-Pro base/zoom scores change from 45.2/58.6 in v1 to 49.8/57.0 for v3-lite and 53.8/61.5 for the expanded model. These are updated results under revised settings, not controlled before-and-after gains. v3 adds UI-Vision 60.0, MMBench-GUI-L2 79.1, and extensive pruning, verifier and timing results. Existing comparator entries also change, including GUI-Actor-3B's ScreenSpot-v2 average from 90.4 to 91.0.

T1.justification: The principal aggregation, similarity, patch-label and loss equations are mathematically retained despite reorganization. v3 removes the alternative distribution-matching definition in v1 Equation 11 and adds a complexity argument reducing attention extraction from O((|V|+|Q|+1)^2) to O((|Q|+1)|V|). No theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The core claims about coordinate-free intrinsic-attention grounding, anchor aggregation and data-efficient fine-tuning remain. v3 adds an explicit claim of scalability through additional desktop-domain training data and extends its headline performance claims to five benchmarks.

C2.justification: v3 substantially expands the mechanism interpretation: visual-sink tokens are described as functional cross-modal proxies that need not be semantically informative, and anchor-weight similarity supports that explanation. Section 4.5 interprets layer/head contributions and pruning outcomes. The results discussion adds data-scaling interpretations and explicitly qualifies UI-Vision results as in-domain, while the soft-variant tradeoff discussion disappears.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents FlashAttention combined with eager extraction of selected attention rows, a 28×28 patch setting, measured GPU-hours and inference times, and the sources of UI-Vision/MMBench comparator scores. The existing hardware, batch size, learning rate, anchor-token formatting and project access link are retained.

R1.justification: The central positioning against TAG and GUI-Actor remains largely unchanged. Citations expand to support newer comparators, datasets and implementation, including Qwen3-VL, GroundCUA/GroundNext, FlashAttention, UI-Vision and MMBench-GUI. Samaran et al. replaces the Nguyen et al. attention-supervision citation, and the GUI-ARP reference is removed.

P1.justification: The introduction and methodological exposition are extensively rewritten. v1's five method subsections become three reorganized subsections, combining preliminaries with anchor aggregation and grouping labeling with training/inference design. Experimental organization, the abstract, conclusion and appendix structure are also revised substantially.

P2.justification: Benchmark tables are expanded and regrouped, with denser layouts and inline citations. v3 adds Tables 3 and 7–10, token-frequency and head-weight figures, and a new similarity visualization replacing v1 Figure 5. The zoom-analysis table replaces accuracy with net-improvement counts and relabels Relax@2 as Relax@3. Pipeline graphics, convergence curves and qualitative grounding examples are retained or relocated.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for the central design and efficiency claims. Larger-data controls give GUI-Actor the same weighted labels, addressing a comparison confound, while stopped-gradient tests, head pruning and measured training/inference costs address questions left largely unresolved by v1's small-data ablations and convergence plots. Broader comparisons and clearer exposition add value. Inconsistent training counts, unexplained score revisions and overbroad state-of-the-art wording remain weaknesses—for example, UI-Vision's 60.0 trails GroundNext-3B's 62.1—but the added validation provides a substantial net improvement.
